text.cuttack: Insight reportWhat should I know about Cuttack?From the findings already minedCuttack’s sample covers 1,104 activities in Dadhapatna and Govindapur, with activity volumes nearly even at 565 and 539 respectively. Planned cost is Rs 5.35 crore, while recorded spending is Rs 2.17 crore, leaving spending Rs 3.18 crore below plan. Govindapur holds 56.2% of planned cost but accounts for 65.3% of the below-plan amount, or Rs 2.07 crore; its spending-to-plan ratio is 30.9%. Dadhapatna accounts for 57.1% of spending and 61.9% of the 181 ongoing activities.Plans are strongly oriented towards infrastructure and public works. Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—accounts for 84.3% of the Rs 3.69 crore untied grant planned, despite representing 43.6% of activities. Public Works comprise 88.5% of all planned activities, or 977 activities. The Rs 1.65 crore tied-grant plan is almost entirely split between Drinking water at 51.8% (Rs 85.61 lakh) and Sanitation at 48.2% (Rs 79.71 lakh), while the other 23 focus-area values together account for only Rs 1,000. Of all planned activities, 57.9% are costed and 42.1% are costless.Record linkage and sanction details merit reconciliation. Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 2.07 crore, and the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across six years; however, Cuttack does not follow the increasing calendar-quarter pattern seen in 6/9 districts. Sanctioning authority is not recorded for 923 rows, which account for 94.1% of the Rs 3.18 crore below-plan amount, or Rs 2.99 crore. The sanction-based comparison covers only activities with a sanction record—about one in six—and shows spending Rs 18.73 lakh below sanction; Dadhapatna accounts for Rs 11.79 lakh and Govindapur for Rs 6.94 lakh.as of 2026-09-11
text.chikilli: Insight reportHow is Chikilli doing?From the findings already minedChikilli has planned 640 activities costing Rs 5.51 crore across 28 focus areas, with no single area dominant; maintenance of community systems accounts for 23.1% of planned cost and roads for 17.5%. However, spending is Rs 4.12 crore below plan, while recorded spending across 6 fiscal years totals Rs 1.39 crore. Within the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample, Chikilli has the lowest sanctioned amount and proposed cost at sanction across all fiscal years, and the lowest numbers of activities with technical and administrative approval in 5/6 fiscal years; 2023-2024 is the exception, with no clear pattern.Activity and expenditure records warrant reconciliation. Although 85.9% of planned activities—550 of 640—are recorded as “Activity Approved,” only 65 activities are ongoing. In the general-component status breakdown, ongoing works account for 93.1% of spending, or Rs 1.52 crore, while representing 10.2% of the 640 activities. Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 1.30 crore, and the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across 6 fiscal years; this may reflect improved recording completeness unless the cashbook total rose alongside it.Record quality and stalled works are additional review points. Nearly two-thirds of planned activities are uncategorised—64.4%, or 412 activities—limiting visibility into the asset mix. Planned money on abandoned works totals Rs 46.72 lakh, led by Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village at Rs 20.44 lakh and Theme 5—Clean and Green Village at Rs 15.77 lakh. Among ongoing activities, drinking water and sanitation each account for 15 activities, making these useful areas for field verification alongside the approval, sanction and expenditure records.as of 2026-09-11

text.mostly_patterns: Insight reportWhich places are behaving differently from the rest?From the findings already minedChikilli repeatedly departs from the pattern seen elsewhere in the sample. While 19/20 Gram Panchayats show an even spread of spending against plan across fund components, Chikilli does not; it also differs from the 19/20 with an even spread of spending against sanction across focus areas and fiscal years. Chikilli is also uneven across activity statuses and types of work when spending is assessed against sanction. These findings concern how spending is distributed across categories, not the amount spent.Laxmipur and Boipariguda show narrower but recurring differences. Laxmipur is uneven across activity statuses when spending is assessed against both plan and sanction, and across types of work under both measures. Boipariguda is uneven across activity statuses under both measures.Output-type patterns provide a further set of exceptions. Code 101 and Code 105 have the lowest spending against plan in 17/20 Gram Panchayats; Boipariguda and Karuabahal instead have Code 101 and Code 103 lowest, while Haldikudar has Code 101 and Code 104 lowest. Against sanction, Code 101 is lowest in 19/20 Gram Panchayats, with no clear pattern in Chikilli.as of 2026-09-11
